problems.description: Mechanical convention score of 0.53 with 34 violations conflicts with the actual diff. Listed violations (e.g. 'index.ts: Classes should use PascalCase' where index.ts is a single export line) are false positives from naive static analysis; the real code is consistently camelCase functions, PascalCase types, 2-space indent, single quotes.
Page.outputPath stores a relative path resolved only later in buildSite, while its name implies an absolute output path; a comment or rename would remove the ambiguity.
escapeHtml is applied to titles and metadata but page.html from marked is emitted raw; acceptable for a local SSG but unescaped Markdown renderer output should be documented as trusted input.
Cognitive complexity +12 driven by buildSite's inline directory-write loop; extracting a writePage helper would flatten it.

strengths: Clean greenfield layering: cli.ts (IO/arg parsing) vs site-generator.ts (pure build logic) vs index.ts (public API) is a sound architectural split with good separation of concerns.
CLI errors go to stderr with non-zero exit codes; usage() on bad command and per-option validation are correct Unix conventions.
Recursive directory walk is async and non-blocking; Promise.all over pages keeps the build parallel.
Escaping of user-controlled title/metadata in generated HTML plus encodeURI on hrefs is proper hygiene.
Tests are well-factored (temporaryDirectory helper, frontmatter/fallback-title coverage) and jest/ts-jest config is minimal and idiomatic.
commit_reviews.summary: Well-structured greenfield commit; the 0.53 convention score is contradicted by the diff (listed violations are static-analysis false positives on files without classes), and actual adherence is good, so treat the mechanical score with skepticism.

problems.description: Module-level WeakMap (pageFrontmatter) stores frontmatter context keyed by Page object; the same data could be passed directly to renderWithTemplates since Page already carries template/layout, making the indirection hard to reason about and easy to break if Page lifetime assumptions change.

The Handlebars-compatible renderer implements only a subset (if/each/partials/triple-stash); {{else}} branches are not handled and would be emitted as literal template text, silently producing wrong output for real Handlebars templates. Compatibility claim is overbroad.

loadTemplates re-reads the templates/partials/layouts directories from disk for every page inside renderWithTemplates, so build cost is O(pages x template files) instead of loading once per buildSite call.
renderWithTemplates returns undefined when no template resolves and none is explicitly set, silently skipping templating; a fallback or explicit error path would be more predictable.

strengths: Templating is a natural, conventional extension for a static site generator: frontmatter-driven template/layout selection plus separate templates/partials/layouts directories mirrors established SSG patterns (Eleventy/Jekyll/Hugo).
No new runtime dependencies introduced — the template engine is self-contained, consistent with the generator's zero-plugin posture.
New code follows existing conventions: camelCase functions, PascalCase types, async/promise flow, and BuildOptions defaults via path.resolve mirrors the existing buildSite structure.
Graceful handling of missing templates directory (ENOENT returns empty map) and clear errors for explicitly requested-but-missing templates.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured, convention-consistent feature addition for an SSG, but it ships a partial custom template engine with a WeakMap indirection and per-page template reloads that constitute modest technical debt — and note the mechanical convention score of 0.53 reflects pre-existing violations in untouched files (index.ts, dev-server.ts), not this commit, which introduces none.

problems.description: dev-server.ts (WebSocket live-reload, path-traversal guard, rebuild debounce) ships with no test coverage, unlike the rest of the module which is jest-tested.

Mechanical convention score is 0.53 (34 violations), but every flagged rule (Classes/Interfaces PascalCase, Functions camelCase, snake_case) is satisfied by the new code in this diff — the listed violations in cli.ts/dev-server.ts/index.ts appear to be false positives or pre-existing, not introduced by this commit.
Injected reload script is a single opaque minified string and the rebuild queueing/debounce logic is hand-rolled rather than using a scheduler utility.

strengths: Integrates cleanly with the existing architecture: reuses buildSite and BuildOptions instead of duplicating build logic, and the serve command mirrors the build command's CLI structure.
Path-traversal protection (403 on paths escaping outputDir) shows security awareness in the new static file serving.
Correct resource lifecycle: close() tears down watcher, WebSocket server, and HTTP server; rebuild handles concurrent triggers with a pending flag.
Respects existing patterns: new module exported through index.ts via export *, options parsing extended with an allowPort flag rather than rewritten.
Mechanical measurements support the change: +0 bugs, +0 smells, +0.0% duplication, only +1 cognitive complexity for 141 added lines.
commit_reviews.summary: High architectural fit — the dev server slots into the existing SSG pipeline cleanly and shows good lifecycle/security discipline — but the mechanical convention score of 0.53 is a discrepancy, since the specific violations reported do not match any code actually added in this commit.

problems.description: The new Plugin lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onFile/onEnd) is not wired into the build pipeline — buildSite is untouched, and DevServerPlugin.start() calls buildSite directly, bypassing the hooks it defines. The plugin system is a facade, not an integration.

plugin.ts resolveBuildOptions re-implements default resolution (contentDir/outputDir/templatesDir/defaultTemplate/configFile/plugins) that site-generator already performs, creating a second source of truth that can drift (matches SonarQube +1 smell, +16 cognitive complexity).
PluginModule union type (Plugin | factory | { default } | { plugins[] }) is broad and loosely typed, inviting misuse of export shapes across markdown/template plugins.
Refactor of dev-server and new plugin surface ships with no test changes despite a public-API-adjacent change (+4 files, +25 imports).

Convention score 0.53 (34 violations) is dominated by pre-existing violations in cli.ts and index.ts that this commit does not touch; the new code itself uses PascalCase classes and camelCase functions correctly. Flagging as discrepancy: the measurement overstates this commit's own non-adherence.

strengths: Backward-compatible move — src/dev-server.ts re-exports from plugins/dev-server, preserving the existing public API for downstream consumers.
Follows existing repository patterns (barrel re-export via index.ts, interface-first API typing).
Clean seam for future extensibility: the onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onFile/onEnd hook surface is a sensible plugin contract.
Mechanically low-risk: net-zero line delta (+268/-267), 0 new bugs, 0.0% duplication.
commit_reviews.summary: A backward-compatible, low-risk reorganization that introduces a plugin seam but ships it as an unintegrated facade with duplicated option resolution, leaving the new lifecycle hooks dead until buildSite is updated.

problems.description: Cache invalidation keys only on source content + template hashes; changes to configFile or plugin configuration produce stale pages without a rebuild because plugin identity/config are not part of the cache key.

Cached Page objects are serialized to JSON in the manifest, so plugin-injected state on pages is lost on reload; skipped pages pushed from cache on subsequent builds may differ from freshly rendered ones.
readManifest silently returns undefined on any parse/corruption error (all catch branches swallow the error), so a corrupted .ssg-cache.json rebuilds everything with no diagnostic.
The manifest stores renderedHtml for every built page, duplicating output content in .ssg-cache.json, which grows unboundedly with content size.
--clean removes only the cache file, but orphaned-output cleanup is gated on previousManifest being present (undefined after clean), so --clean leaves stale output HTML files behind.

strengths: Incremental build with per-source SHA-256 + template hash invalidation and a versioned cache manifest (version: 1) for forward compatibility
Automatically removes output files for deleted sources via currentSources tracking
Extends BuildOptions/BuildResult and follows existing patterns: plugin lifecycle, `??` fallbacks, and ENOENT handling consistent with surrounding code
Build stats surfaced consistently through BuildResult and the CLI output
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a solid incremental-build feature that cleanly extends existing patterns with a reasonable cache design, but introduces stale-output risk because invalidation ignores config/plugin changes, and the low 0.53 convention score reflects pre-existing violations in untouched files (index.ts, dev-server.ts) rather than this diff's new code.

compounding_issues: The seed codebase was an unrelated Express/JWT auth API; the agent abandoned it entirely in Session 1 and greenfielded an SSG from scratch, so zero seed code was carried forward (harness mismatch absorbed by a fresh build rather than repurposed).

No test runner (npm/node/pytest) was ever available in the sandbox across all 5 sessions, so every session's test suite was written but never executed — verification debt accumulated monotonically and was never cleared.

Session 4's refactor introduced implicit side-channel coupling between the pipeline and plugins (a WeakMap of rendered HTML and `setMarkdownSource` monkeypatching on Page objects) that the Session 5 cache relies on; it works but makes the data flow non-obvious and fragile for future plugins.
Session 4 deleted most of the working dev-server implementation (111 lines removed, 49-line plugin wrapper) in a single large refactor commit, concentrating regression risk in one step.
key_decisions: Greenfielding a fresh Markdown static-site generator in Session 1 rather than adapting the unrelated auth-API seed, defining the entire architecture trajectory.

Hand-rolling a small Handlebars-compatible template renderer (if/each blocks, partials, layouts) in Session 2 instead of adding a templating dependency, keeping runtime deps to just gray-matter and marked.
Integrating a chokidar + WebSocket live-reload dev server in Session 3 with path-traversal protection, adding chokidar/ws as the only new deps.

Introducing a Plugin lifecycle architecture in Session 4 (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) and extracting markdown/template/dev-server into `src/plugins/`, the most consequential structural decision.
Adding `ssg.config.ts/.js` config loading with TS transpileModule support in Session 4, enabling external plugin configuration.

Implementing content-addressed incremental builds in Session 5 via sha256 source/template hashing plus a `.ssg-cache.json` manifest with `--incremental`/`--clean` flags and build stats — a genuine cross-cutting concern layered on the plugin pipeline.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across all five sessions. Session 1 established a clean, well-typed core (markdown parsing, recursive discovery, index generation) with tests; Session 2 extended it cleanly with a dependency-free template engine; Session 3 integrated a polished dev server with live reload. Session 4 was the riskiest point — a ~700-line churn refactor that replaced the monolithic generator with a plugin lifecycle and extracted built-ins — and it succeeded, restructuring rather than degrading the codebase and preserving the public API. Session 5 capped the arc with incremental caching, template-aware invalidation, deleted-page cleanup, and build statistics, all layered cleanly on the Session 4 plugin architecture. The persistent weakness was verification: no test toolchain existed in the environment, so tests grew in volume and sophistication but were never executed, leaving every session's assertions unvalidated.
story_review.summary: A textbook-quality multi-session progression — greenfield core, feature addition, integration, plugin refactor, and cross-cutting caching — that grew in structural sophistication with each commit, held back only by the total absence of runnable test verification.
